trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied value can alter the DQL that a tool executes is decided while each capability assembles its query string: timeframe, additionalFilter, entityNames, clusterId/kubernetesEntityId and eventType are concatenated into template literals and handed to executeDql, with no parameterisation and no check at the MCP tool boundary (zod schemas only type the values as free-form z.string()).

landing_point.why: The advisory is about parameters that are not documented as DQL, and `timeframe` is the first such parameter in the tool schemas: declared as a bare z.string() with only prose about accepted units, and the same free-form field is repeated for list_vulnerabilities, list_problems, get_kubernetes_events and list_exceptions, so a summary-only engineer greps `timeframe` and lands here first.

fix_sites.module_kind: capability / DQL builder (also restructured in the fix)

fix_sites.entry_point: shared helper module reached from all five tools (new file src/utils/dql-sanitize.ts)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared util (new module in the fix)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The smartscapeNodes search is a best-effort path whose errors are deliberately swallowed and which falls back to the classic entity fetch (the code even says smartscapeNodes may not be ready for all environments/users), so a solver can argue it is an optional pre-check rather than a real search route the protection must cover.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: additionalFilter is a bare DQL expression, not a quoted literal — every documented example contains double quotes (vulnerability.risk.level == "CRITICAL", entity_tags == array("dt.owner:team-foo")), so a blanket quote-escaping or quote-rejecting fix turns all documented filters into invalid DQL; the kind of sanitisation has to differ per syntactic position (duration for timeframe, expression check for additionalFilter, literal escaping for entityNames, ids). Adjacent trap on the same sink: entityNames must be escaped per element before the '*" OR "*' join, because escaping the joined string also escapes the join's own quotes and breaks the existing multi-name OR search test at src/capabilities/find-monitored-entity-by-name.test.ts:53-60.

O6_input_shapes: single duration string in an unquoted expression position: timeframe ('24h', '7d', '30d')
array of name strings joined into one wildcard OR search: entityNames (string[]), escaped per element before the '*" OR "*' join (fix.diff:37-44), not after it
free-form DQL filter expression appended after '| filter', optionally absent: additionalFilter
optional identifier strings in any present/absent combination: clusterId and kubernetesEntityId, where the fix also stops emitting '== "undefined"' for the missing one
enum-constrained single value still placed inside a quoted literal: eventType (z.enum at src/index.ts:1075-1092), escaped although the schema already restricts it
value with a backslash immediately before a quote ('foo\\"bar'), where escape order matters (backslashes first, then quotes)

O7_producer.where: src/index.ts:406-428 (timeframe and additionalFilter are z.string() with no pattern, defaults applied in the schema); the fix deliberately does not rely on it and re-checks inside each capability function, which the tool handlers call at src/index.ts:441, 518, 575/602, 1100 and 1348

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a numeric-looking parameter interpolated unquoted into the DQL (riskScore: 'vulnerability.risk.score >= ${riskScore || 8.0}')
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer adding a minRiskScore or a result-limit parameter writes it exactly the way timeframe was written, and a string-typed or coerced limit would land directly in the query

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the tool's 'Next Steps' response builds a DQL template with ${timeframe} and tells the model to run it through execute_dql (repeated at src/index.ts:533 and src/index.ts:1114)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: extending a tool's follow-up guidance by copying an existing template is the established pattern in this file, and a new template that embeds a per-call value would sit outside every capability-level check

O8b_injection_room.sibling: arbitrary DQL text persisted into a notebook section (item.text at src/capabilities/notebooks.ts:30)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer adding a 'save this analysis as a notebook' helper would template the caller's parameters into the stored DQL the same way the list_* tools do

O8b_injection_room.sibling: timeframeStart/timeframeEnd currently passed as structured analyzer parameters; a DQL-templating analyzer path would embed them like list_problems does
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the analyzer call already carries a timeframe per call, so wiring it into a DQL string is a small and plausible maintainer change on the same sink family

O9_family: query-language injection: CWE-943 improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic (DQL injection)

There is no unit test for list_vulnerabilities, list_problems, list_exceptions or get_events_for_cluster at the pinned commit; integration-tests/*.integration.test.ts need a live Dynatrace tenant and are a separate jest project.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten the MCP field instead of the query builder: add z.string().regex(/^[1-9]\d*[smhdwMy]$/) to `timeframe` in src/index.ts and call it done — that leaves additionalFilter, clusterId/kubernetesEntityId, entityNames and the exported capability functions untouched, and a quote-escaping-only variant leaves timeframe injectable because it is interpolated into an expression, not a string literal.

out_of_scope_notes: src/index.ts:745-768: the execute_dql tool passes a caller-supplied DQL statement verbatim to executeDql, which is that tool's documented contract and outside this advisory's 'parameters not documented as DQL' property; noted, not pursued.

src/capabilities/send-event.ts:37-38 and src/capabilities/notebooks.ts:44: user strings reach other query-ish sinks (events ingest entitySelector, notebook content); different sinks from the DQL execution path, noted, not pursued.

The advisory body beyond the one-line summary was not available; the reading of which parameters count as 'not documented as DQL' comes from the tool schema descriptions (additionalFilter is documented as DQL, timeframe/entityNames/clusterId/eventType are not).

The published fix also changes get_events_for_cluster behaviour beyond injection (clusterId/kubernetesEntityId become optional and a filter is emitted only for supplied ids, instead of '== "undefined"' for the missing one); whether the benchmark report states that requirement is unknown, and the fix's new test src/capabilities/get-events-for-cluster.test.ts asserts it.
